Aa

Macrons

Consonantal i

Consonantal u

Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

innocent adjective

also not guilty, acquitted, blameless, innocence, acquit, acquittal, acquit of a capital crime, be acquitted, hung jury, acquitted by a hung jury, not at fault

classical

Cic. Tusc. 5.41
Cic. Rosc. Am. 56
Traupman 195, 154

innocēns, innocentis

innocent, blameless; harmless

Properly ‘doing no harm’, in- and nocēns (Cic. Tusc. 5.41); of the accused, not guilty. Of what, in the genitive (Tac. Ann. 4.34, Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • īnsōns, īnsontis — guiltless, innocent

    also used · classical · Sall. Cat. 16.3 (Lewis & Short); Liv. 22.49 (Lewis & Short); Hor. S. 1.6.69 (Lewis & Short)

    Not in Cicero or Caesar; Plautus, Sallust, Livy and the poets (Lewis & Short).

  • absolvō, absolvere, absolvī, absolūtum — acquit, find not guilty

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Rosc. Am. 56: absolvī potest; Traupman 191, 193; Traupman 193: acquit

    Of a charge, with dē and the ablative, more rarely the genitive (Traupman 193).

  • innocentia, innocentiae f. — innocence, integrity

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Traupman 154

  • absolūtiō, absolūtiōnis f. — an acquittal

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Clu. 27: sententiīs decem et sex absolūtiō cōnficī poterat (Lewis & Short); Traupman 193; Cic. Clu. 74: absolūtiō cōnficī poterat (Lewis & Short); Traupman 268

Examples

  • haec propter illōs scrīpta est hominēs fābula quī fictīs causīs innocentēs opprimunt

    this fable was written for those people who crush the innocent with made-up chargesPhaedr. 1.1.14–15

  • innocēns is dīcitur, nōn quī leviter nocet, sed quī nihil nocet

    a man is called innocent not if he does little harm, but if he does noneCic. Tusc. 5.41

  • aliquem capitis absolvere

    to acquit someone of a capital crimeTraupman 193

  • sententiīs paribus absolvī

    to be acquitted by a hung jury (by an equal vote)Traupman 195

  • Absolūtus est omnibus sententiīs.

    He was acquitted unanimously.Traupman 191

  • extrā culpam esse

    not to be at faultTraupman 195

See also guilty, trial.
